title: emma sullivan - sre oncall scratchpad 2026-03-18
content:
03/18/2026 - Oncall notes (EMMA)

02:14 UTC - Pager: INC-4357 - high CPU on ded-rt-2 (prod-us-west)
- Alert: cpu_utilization > 92% across all pods in GPU pool ded-rt-2 for 3m
- Immediate actions: rotated traffic off node-7, scaled up pool by +2 nodes via autoscaler (worked), restarted affected serving pods
- Mitigation outcome: CPU dropped to ~48% within 4m, request latency returned to normal
- Notes: node-7 shows GPU driver OOM warnings; disk pressure low. Suspect degraded model shard placement + kernel mem leak.
- Follow-ups:
  * INC-4357 owner: Emma Sullivan (me)
  * Postmortem: start draft tomorrow, assign infra lead Aditi for kernel investigation
  * Runbook TODO: add a step to drain node and collect nvidia-smi + dmesg on GPU OOM alerts
  * Add metric: GPU driver OOM count -> alert when >0 in 5m
  * File ticket to investigate autoscaler behavior when node removal occurs (JIRA:INC-4358)

04:50 UTC - Paging note: brief spike in request 5xx for hosted-api route /v1/generate
- Correlated with upstream model shard failover during ded-rt-2 event
- Mitigation: enabled fallback routing to model-variant: gpt-small-v2 in routing policy for 8m
- Action: add a canary rule in routing config to avoid full traffic switch for single-pool incidents

Runbook quick items (to capture while fresh):
- When GPU driver OOM observed:
  1) Drain node (kubectl cordon + drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data)
  2) Collect: /var/log/syslog, dmesg, nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/gpu-dump
  3) Archive dump to s3://redwood-ops/oncall-dumps/<node>-<date>
  4) Reboot node if driver continues to OOM after restart of driver
  5) Notify infra on-call and tag Aditi
- Add to runbook: sample kubectl commands and a link to driver binary version matrix

Outstanding TODOs (priority order):
- [P0] Create INC-4358 with autoscaler attach/detach timeline + logs (assigned to Noah) -> due 03/19
- [P0] Draft postmortem for INC-4357 (me) -> publish by 03/20
- [P1] Update oncall runbook with GPU OOM collection steps (me + Harper) -> 03/21
- [P1] Add Prometheus alert for nvidia_driver_oom_total > 0 in 5m (alerts owner: infra-alerts)
- [P2] Add routing canary rule to avoid whole-pool fallback for hosted-api (product + infra) -> spike doc

Notes to self / rough commands used:
- kubectl get pods -n svc-ded-rt-2 -o wide | grep CrashLoop
- kubectl cordon node-7 && kubectl drain node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- autoscaler scale --pool ded-rt-2 --delta 2 --reason "oncall emergency scale"
- /scripts/collect-gpu-diagnostics.sh node-7 /tmp/gpu-dump && aws s3 cp /tmp/gpu-dump s3://redwood-ops/oncall-dumps/

Slack & comms:
- Posted incident summary in #infra-incidents and #prod-alerts (pinned threads)
- Notified CSE on call for customer-impacting inquiries (no customer-facing incident required)

Quick retrospective: autoscaler reacted but node with driver OOM reintroduced instability; need a pre-drain health check before returning node to scheduler. Also consider a grace-window when scaling down to avoid reassigning shards to unstable nodes.

End of shift handoff:
- Handoff to Aditi (kernel trace) and Noah (autoscaler logs). See linked artifacts.
- If more paging fires for ded-rt-2, escalate to on-call manager.
